title: Prove eight bits are necessary for algebra-faithful affine A5 actions
body:
Nick Petalas's #5114 constructs an algebra-faithful A5 action on eight binary address bits and leaves the minimum over all affine representations open. This proves **eight is the minimum**, including nonsplit representations and affine actions without a fixed point. It answers that PR's Open next question 2; its eight-bit upper construction retains full credit.

The new reduction covers every relevant module, rather than sampling smaller candidates. An exact quotient of F2[A5] identifies all simple modules (dimensions 1, 4, 4), with kernel powers of dimensions `35,27,17,9,0`. Every module with one nontrivial composition factor is a subquotient of one of two explicit universal eight-dimensional extensions, plus fixed summands. Their actions on all 256 vectors have algebra ranks **52 and 34**, with explicit nonzero annihilators. An affine action on at most seven bits homogenizes to a module of dimension at most eight with a trivial quotient, so it falls under this obstruction. The written proof includes the nonsplit, subquotient and affine-slice steps.

Only seven files in `research/a5-affine-address-minimum/` are added. The complete proof is in its README; the finite quotient has a separately implemented checker. Both implementations explicitly reconcile their natural-module coordinate bases.

Validation at `6779a28938a9af1ba3d32e18ba8feb8d7cc002f8`:

- CPython 3.12, standard library: registered warning-strict normal and optimized replays pass. Every group product, universal-action kernel witness and the matching regular-orbit fixture is checked exactly. There are 14 rejecting controls, plus 256 P/Q cases and 44,032 subquotient domain points per module.
- Metadata and exact source pins pass. Committed bytes and source ancestry pass for all nine package/input files.
- The official export passes its integrity check. Both direct modes pass with Git absent from PATH and all exported files read-only; all ten exported files, including the export receipt, remain byte-identical.
- Export SHA256: `824e7b6363787a4ef6bd3e92cbfda576436f850b8a0fef246931bf57f6554f4e`.

Fresh canonical base and pre-submission refresh: `20a1e31bc6009b9b3f4d084bbaadc6350e34fcba`, priority revision 7. [Canonical claim #5131](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5131). The pre-submission overlap refresh covers 318 open PRs, 4,290 Discussion records, 4,406 closed PRs and the complete main-tree note inventory, supplemented by targeted live PR/Discussion checks. No competing minimum claim surfaced; unpublished work and arbitrary diffs are outside that coverage.

Limitations: this is an author-checked scoped proof with exact finite ingredients, not a proof-kernel formalization or independent human acceptance. Arbitrary nonlinear address actions, optimal CNOT counts, a source-bound physical BIT caller, movement/restoration tariffs, recursive admission and a new kappa remain unclaimed. The selected frontier and frozen predecessor sources are unchanged. The remaining useful task is #5114's actual caller and complete-bill question, explicitly left unreserved.

Prepared by Krzysztof Wojt with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including a Luna finite-algebra implementation and proof-gap review. Credit Nick Petalas #5114; Wentao Li #4089; Cinna Davis #2246/#3914; the classical A5/SL2(F4) and module-theoretic methods; and the retained register-model lineage, including eumemic and Ali Romman. Apache-2.0.

Hosted CI is pending; the evidence above is local.
